course_name_original: Certificación Energética y Energías Renovables en la Edificación
course_name_en: Energy Certification and Renewable Energies in Buildings

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and apply European Directives and Spanish regulations aimed at energy saving and improving energy efficiency in buildings.
Evaluate available geothermal, aerothermal, and solar resources for use in building thermal systems in a given area or environment.
Design basic equipment and systems for building thermal installations.

Analyze practical cases of energy evaluation in buildings, assessing energy savings and CO2 emission reductions obtained with different technological solutions, particularly with the use of renewable resource utilization technologies.
Use simulation software tools as support for studying the thermal behavior of buildings and for energy certification.

syllabus_topics: Evolution in Europe and Spain of energy demand and the use of renewable energies in buildings (European Directives). Spanish Regulations: Technical Building Code (CTE) and Regulation of Thermal Installations in Buildings (RITE).
Methodology for energy certification analysis in buildings. Case studies.
Simulation software tools for studying the thermal behavior of buildings.
Renewable technologies in buildings_1: heat pump (aerothermal and geothermal) and biomass.
Renewable technologies in buildings_2: Solar energy.
Thermal energy recovery in ventilation systems and sensible and latent heat storage.

assessment_methods.method: Active participation (PA): Completion of in-person seminar practices and exercises assigned by the professor.
Individual work (TI): A report or practical case (pre-project type) completed by the student throughout the course, autonomously or in groups.
Laboratory practices (PL): Resolution of questionnaires related to established practices.
Theoretical-practical exam (EX): A written test covering theoretical content and associated practical considerations.

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.15 x (PA) + 0.20 x (TI) + 0.20 x PL + 0.45 x (EX). A final grade of 5 points is required to pass the subject. For students with Differentiated Evaluation, PA is replaced by an additional individual assignment and PL is replaced by an extra exam on the same day as the general exam. For extraordinary evaluation, the individual work (TI) must still be submitted (or a new one, with a deadline one week before the exam), and the final exam will cover both theoretical-practical (EX) and laboratory practice (PL) content, with the formula being 0.20 x (TI) + 0.20 x (PL) + 0.60 x (EX). A final grade of 5 points is required.
